problem: Learned visual odometry (VO) models for GPS-free PointNav use CNNs with fixed input channels (RGB-D), so they fail catastrophically (collapse to blind behaviour) when a sensor drops out or the sensor suite changes, and they need millions of simulator samples to train.
motivation: Real robots face sensor failures, bandwidth or power limits and different sensor suites, so a reusable VO model must tolerate missing modalities. Transformers accept variable token sets and can start from multi-modal pre-training, which should cut data needs.
key_idea: A ViT-based VO Transformer (VOT) with an action token fed into the encoder, MultiMAE pre-training, and random modality dropping during training makes one model invariant to which of RGB/depth is available.
insight: Table 2 shows that MultiMAE pre-training and the action-token prior are complementary (rows 10 vs 13 vs 16: S 72.1 -> 85.7 -> 88.2). Invariance training lets a single RGB-D model match single-modality models when a modality is dropped (drop RGB: S 91.0; drop depth: 60.9, versus 26.1 without invariance training), while the CNN baseline gets S 0.0. Depth is far more informative than RGB (RGB-only overfits appearance), and attention maps show the action token steers attention to regions shared across both frames.
method: VOT backbone: ViT-B (patch 16, 12 blocks, dim 768) on the pair of frames o_t and o_{t+1}, with separate linear patch projections per modality and 2D sin-cos positional embeddings. Observations are resized to 160x80 and modalities are concatenated along height.

Action token: the discrete action is embedded and passed as a token into the encoder (not concatenated to the features afterwards), conditioning feature extraction on the action; its output token feeds the head.
VO head: a 2-layer MLP (GELU, hidden 384) on the output token predicts the SE(2) transform (rotation β and translation ξ). The relative goal is then updated as g_{t+1}=H·g_t.

MultiMAE pre-training: initialised from the public MultiMAE (RGB+depth+semseg) weights, with the semseg projections discarded, then fine-tuned. Only 250k training pairs are used, against 1M and 5M for prior work.
Modality-invariance training: each batch draws a modality combination from a multinomial (RGB 20%, depth 30%, RGB-D 50%) and drops the rest, simulating missing sensors.

Loss and augmentation: L2 loss on ξ and β plus the geometric invariance losses of Zhao et al., with left/right turn augmentation by horizontal flip and inverse transform. The frozen pre-trained Zhao et al. navigation policy consumes the estimated goal.

setting.backbone: ViT-B (MultiMAE-pretrained, fine-tuned) VO model + frozen pre-trained LSTM/ResNet-18 navigation policy
setting.training_data: 250k observation-transformation pairs (25k val) collected in Habitat on Gibson-4+ train scenes; MultiMAE pre-training on ImageNet with pseudo-labels
setting.action_space: discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP (noisy actuation)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT GPS only used to label VO training data)

numbers.method: VOT-B w/ inv. (RGB-D, pretrained, action token)
numbers.backbone: ViT-B MultiMAE-pretrained + policy of Zhao et al.
numbers.extra: 250k training samples; realistic noisy PointNav without GPS; metrics printed as e^-2 (x100)
numbers.evidence: Table 2 row 17 (Ablation study of architecture design and input modalities)

numbers.backbone: ViT-B MultiMAE-pretrained (row 16 model) + Partsey et al. policy
numbers.extra: trained on ~5% of the data of Partsey et al.; leaderboard retrieved 05-Nov-2022

numbers_note: Metrics in Tables 1-2 are printed as e^-2 (x100). Table 1 test-time drop results for VOT w/ inv.: drop RGB S 91.0/SPL 69.4; drop depth S 60.9/SPL 47.2. The Gibson-PointNav bench label is used for the Habitat PointNav Gibson-4+ validation scenes.
results: On Gibson-4+ val, VOT w/ inv. reaches S 92.6 / SPL 70.6 vs 64.5 / 48.9 for the Zhao et al. baseline (row 2), and stays close to the GPS oracle (97.8/74.8). On the Habitat Challenge 2021 test-std leaderboard it ranks first with SoftSPL 77 and on-par SPL 74, using ~5% of Partsey et al.'s data.
limitations: Only the VO model is modality-invariant; the navigation policy still requires depth input.
Assumes accurate sensor-failure detection, an idealised setup; only RGB-D and discrete actions were tested, in simulation.
Depth-drop still degrades performance noticeably (S 60.9), and pre-trained weights may not exist for other sensor types.
builds_on: Zhao et al. 2021 (VO for realistic PointNav)
